deterministic_checks.notes: All body citations [^1]-[^5] resolve. [^6] is listed in References but never cited in the body (orphan). [^5] (rank 6) is cited in a role 3 section. Every ✅ in roles 1-5 carries a citation. sections_present is true for the doc's own concept-doc sections; no section does the role 2 or role 5 job (see diataxis notes).

claim_checks.claim: `private` and `protected` are enforced only during type checking. Runtime lookups, and bracket notation even during type checking, still reach the member: it is "soft private".
claim_checks.page_says: private and protected are only enforced during type checking. … private also allows access using bracket notation during type checking … these fields are soft private
claim_checks.note: The handbook gives the bracket-notation escape and the 'soft private' label for `private` only. The claim's subject is 'private and protected', so it widens both to `protected`. Runtime-lookup part is entailed.

claim_checks.claim: `#` fields stay private after compilation and have no bracket-notation escape hatch: they are "hard private".
claim_checks.page_says: JavaScript’s private fields (#) remain private after compilation and do not provide the previously mentioned escape hatches like bracket notation access, making them hard private.

claim_checks.claim: When compiling to ES2021 or lower, TypeScript replaces `#` with `WeakMap`s. The handbook notes that these runtime privacy checks will degrade performance.
claim_checks.page_says: When compiling to ES2021 or less, TypeScript will use WeakMaps in place of #. … Note that these added privacy checks during runtime could affect performance.
claim_checks.note: First sentence entailed. Second sentence raises the page's 'could affect' to 'will degrade' (a MUST-level 'will'). It also narrows the note to the WeakMap downlevel, while the page says it of hard-privacy mechanisms in general: closures, WeakMaps or private fields.

claim_checks.claim: Private elements are not properties. They cannot be enumerated, deleted, proxied, or reached through `Object` methods, and `structuredClone()` copies them like public fields.
claim_checks.page_says: they cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method. … structuredClone() does not clone private elements
claim_checks.note: The first part is entailed. MDN says the opposite about structuredClone(): private elements are not cloned.

claim_checks.claim: Reading a `#` field from an object whose class did not declare it throws a `TypeError`. `#x in obj` checks for it without throwing.
claim_checks.page_says: access a private element from an object that doesn't have the element, a TypeError is thrown … return true if the private field or method exists, and false otherwise

claim_checks.claim: V8 9.4 moved class-field initialization, including private fields, onto its inline-cache fast path. Before that it went through slower runtime calls.
claim_checks.page_says: Before v9.7, V8 always used a costly runtime call for class field initializations. With v9.7, when V8 considers the pattern … predictable enough, it uses a new IC
claim_checks.note: The page gives v9.7, not 9.4 (the doc's own front matter also says V8 ≥ 9.7). The claim also drops the condition that the IC is used only when the initialization pattern is predictable; otherwise V8 falls back to a runtime call.

claim_checks.claim: An injected collaborator (port, clock, logger) | `private readonly x` constructor parameter | A `#` name cannot be a parameter property
claim_checks.page_says: Allow `#`-private names in parameter property positions … That this is not possible is a bit surprising
claim_checks.note: Entailed by the issue, but [^5] is Rank 6 and role 3 allows ranks 1-4: KB-15 breach recorded separately. The handbook's Parameter Properties section [^1] lists only public, private, protected or readonly as the prefixes and could carry this row instead.

claim_checks.claim: Object wrapped in a `Proxy` (some mocking and reactivity libraries) | `#` access does not go through the proxy | Private elements cannot be proxied
claim_checks.page_says: they cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method.

claim_checks.claim: Target ES2021 or lower | `#` becomes `WeakMap` lookups | TypeScript downlevels it
claim_checks.page_says: When compiling to ES2021 or less, TypeScript will use WeakMaps in place of #.

claim_checks.claim: Working around it with `--experimental-transform-types` | Runs on Node 24.22 with an `ExperimentalWarning` (re-tested 2026-11-03); the flag is removed in Node 26.0.0 | So code meant to run unbuilt keeps injected collaborators as `readonly #field`s assigned in the constructor
claim_checks.note: The removal in 26.0.0 is entailed. The cited page is the Node v26.13.1 docs. It does not describe what the flag transforms or any ExperimentalWarning, and does not cover Node 24.22 (searched 'experimental', 'transform', 'ExperimentalWarning'). That part rests only on the doc's local re-test.

claim_checks.claim: Type stripping itself | Stable (stability 2) since Node 24.12.0 and 25.2.0; no warning since 24.3.0; Node ignores `tsconfig.json` and needs `.ts` extensions in relative imports | Node only deletes types
claim_checks.page_says: v25.2.0, v24.12.0 | Type stripping is now stable. … v24.3.0, v22.18.0 | Type stripping no longer emits an experimental warning. … Node.js ignores tsconfig.json files
claim_checks.note: The page also says file extensions are mandatory in import statements (import './file.ts') and that Node 'is only removing inline types'.

conflicts.topic: Version that put class-field initialization on V8's inline-cache path
conflicts.note: Not a disagreement between sources: the doc contradicts its only cited source and its own front matter. Counted as grounding violation C6, not again under KB-17.

conflicts.loser: doc's own statement 'copies them like public fields' (no source)
conflicts.note: The doc contradicts its cited source. Counted as grounding violation C4, not again under KB-17.

conflicts.winner: [^1] rank 1: hard-privacy mechanisms (closures, WeakMaps or private fields) 'could affect performance'
conflicts.loser: Summary and Takeaways: same cost as public fields on a native target (local measurement on Node 24.22, with [^3] rank 4 on the v9.7 fast path)
conflicts.note: No contradiction: the handbook hedges ('could'), and the doc's claim rests on its own measurement within the front matter's V8 ≥ 9.7 scope. But item 3 misreports the handbook's note as a firm claim about the WeakMap downlevel only (C3).

violations.evidence: The 'Where each form fits' row 'An injected collaborator' cites [^5] (github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/36282, Rank 6) in a role 3 section, which allows ranks 1-4.
C3: item 3 says the handbook notes the checks 'will degrade performance'. [^1] says 'could affect performance', and says it of closures, WeakMaps or private fields in general.
C4: item 4 says structuredClone() copies private elements like public fields. [^2] says 'structuredClone() does not clone private elements'.
C6: item 6 says V8 9.4. [^3] says the fix shipped in V8 v9.7 ('Before v9.7, V8 always used a costly runtime call'), and only when the initialization pattern is predictable.
C1: item 1 extends bracket-notation access during type checking and the 'soft private' label to `protected`. [^1] states both for `private` only.
C10: 'Runs on Node 24.22 with an ExperimentalWarning' sits under ✅[^4], but the cited v26.13.1 page does not mention the warning or Node 24.22. Only the doc's local re-test backs it.
[^6] (github.com/tc39/proposal-class-fields) is never cited in the body, though its entry says 'Backs: How it works 2'; item 2 cites only [^1].
It says 'Verified: 10 claims (✅)', but the body has 11 ✅ marks (How it works items 1-6, one in 'Where each form fits', four in Edge cases).

The 'Where each form fits' table is decision guidance, not mechanism; it belongs in role 6 (Trade-offs). No section does the role 2 job (parts and how they relate) or the role 5 job (exact values and rules); the version facts sit in Edge cases instead.

patch_instructions.action: Row 'An injected collaborator' of 'Where each form fits': replace ✅[^5] with ✅[^1], citing the handbook's Parameter Properties section, and reword the Why cell to 'Parameter properties are created only with public, private, protected or readonly; a `#` name is not one of them'. Item 3, second sentence: replace with 'The handbook notes that hard runtime privacy (closures, WeakMaps or private fields) could affect performance. ✅[^1]'. Drop 'will degrade' and do not tie the note to the WeakMap downlevel alone.

Item 4: replace 'and `structuredClone()` copies them like public fields' with '`structuredClone()` does not clone them, and `Object.freeze()` and `Object.seal()` have no effect on them ✅[^2]'. Consider adding an Edge cases row: a structuredClone() copy loses its `#` fields [^2].

Item 6: change 'V8 9.4' to 'V8 v9.7' and add the condition from [^3]: the new inline cache is used when V8 finds the initialization pattern predictable, and V8 falls back to a runtime call otherwise. Keep 'Before v9.7, V8 always used a costly runtime call' ✅[^3].

Row '--experimental-transform-types': keep '✅[^4]' only on 'the flag is removed in Node 26.0.0'. Mark 'Runs on Node 24.22 with an ExperimentalWarning' as a local re-test (2026-11-03) outside the ✅, or cite the Node 24 version of the TypeScript modules page for it.
